text: A PHP and MySQL web application that connects local fish sellers with buyers for browsing, ordering, and managing fresh seafood listings.
A simpler way to buy and manage fresh seafood

Presented by: [Your Name]
Department: [Your Department]
Academic year: 2026
Introduce the problem: buyers need fresh fish and sellers need a simple online channel. Explain that FreshCatch is designed as a small marketplace, not just a CRUD form.
Why an online fish marketplace is useful
Local fish sellers often depend on walk-in customers or phone calls.
Buyers cannot easily compare availability, price, and seller information.
Fresh stock changes daily, so sellers need direct control over listings.
The marketplace keeps product price, quantity, availability, and seller details in one place.
FreshCatch gives sellers a managed shop and gives buyers a clear flow for discovery, cart, checkout, payment simulation, and order tracking.
State the scope clearly: local sellers, fresh fish stock, buyer ordering, seller fulfillment, and marketplace administration.
Each role has a protected set of actions
Browse products, manage cart, save addresses, use UPI Demo or COD, track orders
Manage shop, add stock, upload fish photos, update listings, fulfill own orders
Approve sellers, manage users and categories, monitor products, orders, and reports
Role-based access control checks permissions in PHP. Hiding a menu item alone does not grant access.
Explain that the PHP session stores the signed-in user role and every protected page calls require_role.
Chosen to match the project requirement and keep the application easy to explain
Interactive checkout total, image preview, confirmations
Emphasize that no framework, Node.js, React, or external payment gateway is required. PHP renders pages and MySQL stores data.
Modular PHP pages reuse shared database, authentication, and layout code
config, PDO database, auth, functions, header/footer
Request flow: browser submits a form → PHP validates session and input → PDO prepared statement reads or writes MySQL → PHP renders the next page.
Explain the separation: public page files handle a workflow, includes keep common logic in one place, and database.php gives a single PDO connection.
Normalized relational structure with parent orders and seller orders
seller fulfillment and historical item price
Key design decision: each order item saves unit_price and line_total at checkout, so old orders remain correct after a seller changes a product price.
Mention primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints, indexes, and the parent order plus seller order model for multi-seller carts.
The buyer can complete a full marketplace journey
Checkout revalidates stock inside a database transaction before reducing product quantity and clearing the cart.
Walk through this slowly. Explain that the final stock check is server-side, even if the cart already checked availability.
The application uses a realistic UI without a real payment gateway

• Displays the actual order total
• Shows freshcatch@upi
• Shows a clearly labelled demo QR
• “I have completed payment” records paid

• Creates the order immediately
• Payment method = COD
• Payment status = pending
• Seller can begin fulfillment
No real money transfers occur. The payment feature exists only to demonstrate an e-commerce flow safely.
Say this explicitly: UPI is a simulated payment feature. It does not integrate a bank, QR payment provider, or transaction API.
Sellers manage only their own shop, listings, images, and relevant orders

Own listings
Own images
Own orders
Seller dashboard shows product count, orders, and delivered sales.
My Listings shows each fish product with its uploaded photo, price, stock, and availability.
Seller can add a fish, replace or remove its photo, change stock, hide a listing, or delete it.
Seller sees only seller_orders assigned to their own seller profile.
Cancelled orders stay locked and cannot be changed by the seller.
Point out seller ownership checks in SQL: products use WHERE id=? AND seller_id=?, and seller orders use WHERE seller_id=?.
The project demonstrates core Web Programming security practices
Ownership checks for orders, products, and addresses
Image type and 2 MB size validation
Database transactions and SELECT ... FOR UPDATE at checkout
No plaintext passwords or real banking integration
Mention admin pages: users, sellers, categories, products, all orders, reports, and dashboard statistics.
Use this checklist during your demo and before submission
Login, search, filter, cart quantity, delivery total, pickup total, UPI Demo, COD, My Orders
Login, add fish, upload image, edit stock, delete listing, update own active order
Login, seller approval, user status, categories, product moderation, orders
Buyer blocked from seller/admin pages, seller blocked from other seller products, cancelled order status locked
If asked how you tested, explain manual functional testing for each role plus PHP syntax checks. Do not claim payment or live server tests beyond what you performed.
A complete mini marketplace built with PHP and MySQL
Relational database design and SQL CRUD
Cart, checkout, order, and stock workflows
File upload validation and daily seller listing management
Responsive HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript
End by inviting questions. Be ready to explain schema relationships, password hashing, prepared statements, and why order_items store historical prices.
